items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And Sun Ra was using Pharoah but Trane was calling him all the time.

ctx.x: Oh when I first moved to New York I started working with Grant Green. Guitarist for Blue Note Records, he played bebop guitar. And he had Bob Cranshaw, Bob

Cunningham and Ben Dixon on drums and on tour instead he got an organ. Then sometimes we would play gigs with an organ. And then I got gigs with Hank Crawford. Now this was ’63. But meanwhile I would take little gigs with Sun Ra, with John Gilmore playing saxophone. Actually John Gilmore had went with Trane — I mean Art Blakey. He went with Art Blakey. And Sun Ra was using Pharoah but Trane was calling him all the time. John Coltrane was calling him all the time. So there I was, about the same age. So they tried…
May I ask if that’s the first time, first significant time that the idea of emotion and expression was introduced to you and came out of your horn?

items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: me and Pharoah, he was a year older than me. He was a year older than I. He was born in ’41, I was born in 1942. And we had gotten to, came to New York on the same day.

ctx.x: My spirituality. You know, so he had to wean me off of that foundation. And then I noticed a lot of guys, he was using a lot of musicians but he liked the guys that didn’t have that foundation so much. You know he gravitated to those guys because it was less work to re-indoctrinate you know. Same with John Coltrane. John Coltrane liked Pharoah because he hadn’t had the bebop foundation so much. Pharoah was like a blues kind of guy from Arkansas. And he was — me and Pharoah, he was a year older than me. He was a…

was hanging out with John Coltrane. John liked him you know. So he did more and more with John and John started using him on gigs and whatnot, and he started touring and whatnot, the rest is history. Now with Sun Ra I used to make fun of Sun Ra but something that I really took serious when I saw he was recording everything you know. Rehearsals. And he had two record labels. You know he was producing and marketing his music, and his music was in the marketplace. Of course it was like a small niche fan base. But it…
